paper.citation: Thronsen et al., Ultramicroscopy 255 (2024) 113861, doi:10.1016/j.ultramic.2023.113861 (CC BY 4.0)
paper.data: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.6645396 (CC BY 4.0, stays out of the repo; read from References/mac4DSTEM/thronsen-datasetA)

datasetA.scanSizeSource: PDF page 3, Section 2 ('A dataset, termed Dataset A containing 512 x 512')
datasetA.stepNmPaperTextSource: PDF page 3 ('The scan step size was chosen to be 4.6 nm')
datasetA.stepNmFileSource: their datasetA_preprocessed.hspy axes (2.4943); the owner settled on it 2026-09-28 believing Fig. 7's scale bar agreed; the 2026-10-22 measurement below says it does not, so it is NOT used (see scale)
datasetA.stride3Source: References/mac4DSTEM/thronsen-datasetA/datasetA_stride3.h5 (every 3rd row and column of the preprocessed cube; no calibration stored, Q = 0.01904 per px from their file)

scale.decision: 4.6 nm per position (the paper's own statement, PDF page 3); the file's 2.4943 nm is not used

measured.method: PDF page 8 rendered at 250 dpi; the three 400 nm scale bars of Fig. 7 are 82, 82 and 81 px (panels a, b, c); panel (c) is registered to ground_truth.hspy by searching its bounds for the best class agreement: 99.81 % of the classified figure pixels equal the truth class, so the panel is exactly the 512 x 512 map, 487 px wide (x 1242..1728, y 196..682 of the 2067 x 2756 image)
measured.uncertaintySource: one pixel on the bar (1.2 %) and on the panel edges (0.2 %)
measured.page: PDF page 8 (Fig. 7); the text on PDF page 3 says 4.6 nm and an area of approximately 2.4 um2, a side of 2.4 um, which is 512 x 4.6 = 2.355 um

scale.consequence: lengths read 1.87 times too short and areal densities 3.5 times too high with the file's step; every number in docs/parity.md from 2026-10-22 uses 4.6 nm (stride 3: 13.8 nm)
scale.flag: the owner's 2026-09-28 decision is reversed on a measurement, not a preference: confirm or overrule

fullResolutionAccuracyPercent.source: the four Zenodo maps (published/datasetA_phasemap_*.hspy) against ground_truth.hspy at the full 512 x 512 with the paper's scorer (determine_accuracy.ipynb: count_nonzero(abs(map - truth)) / (512*512), every class and the 4 'not indexed' truth positions counted); reproduces Table 3 (98.50 / 98.46 / 98.25 / 99.04) to 0.01 pp; pinned by ThronsenParityTests.testThePublishedMapsReproduceTable3AtFullResolution

datasetB.stepNmSource: PDF page 3 ('the scan step size was set to 2.3 nm'); scan size not found in the text, so null

zoneAxisPatterns.labelsNote: the paper lists six unique patterns: one Al, one theta'[001], two theta'<100> and two T1 in-plane variants (PDF page 3); the labels above are the four phase classes of the ground truth map

paperAccuracyPercent.source: Table 3, PDF page 11; accuracy = deviation from the manually built ground truth map (the 'pixel-by-pixel difference', PDF page 3)

publishedMapsAtStride3AccuracyPercent.source: 100 - the per-position error of the four published maps (Zenodo datasetA_phasemap_*.hspy) at [::3, ::3] against truth_stride3.json: 1.56 / 1.51 / 1.70 / 0.95 % (A3a, 2026-09-28; computed by us, not published)

variantsPerClassExpected.source: PDF page 3: one unique in-plane angle for theta'[001], two perpendicular for theta'<100>, two for T1

paperAzimuth.source: PDF page 7 (Section 3.7.2): the ANN stack rotated by phi_A = -29.65 deg counter-clockwise, from the vector matching

feretAngleFamilies.source: PDF page 7 (Section 4.1): T1 projected major axis along [110] and [1-10] of Al, theta'<100> along [100] and [010]: two families 90 deg apart each, 45 deg between the two phases
